title: The Running Median

concept.title: Two heaps around the middle: a max-heap of the lower half and a min-heap of the upper half
body: The *median* of some numbers is the middle one when they are sorted. With an even count there are two middle numbers; here the answer is the **lower** of them, which is the `(count + 1) / 2`-th smallest number (rounded down). A sorted list would give it by index, but inserting into a sorted list costs O(n), too slow for a long stream.

Keep the numbers in **two halves**: a **max-heap `low`** with the smaller half and a **min-heap `high`** with the larger half. Every number in `low` is at most every number in `high`, and `low` has the same size as `high` or one more. Then the top of `low` is the lower median.
Each number costs O(log n). The idea of splitting at the middle with two heaps also answers questions like "the sum of the k smallest numbers" in a stream.

statement: Numbers arrive one by one. After each number, print the median of all numbers so far; if their count is even, print the lower one of the two middle numbers (after 2 and 5 the answer is 2).
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers, in the order in which they arrive.
outputFormat: `n` lines: the lower median after every number.
hints: Keep the smaller half in a max-heap and the larger half in a min-heap.
Push the new number into the correct half, then balance so that the lower half has the same size or one more.
The top of the lower half is the answer.

explanation: A max-heap holds the smaller half and a min-heap the larger half, kept balanced so the lower half is never smaller and at most one bigger. The top of the lower half is the lower median.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

import heapq
low, high, out = [], [], []
for x in a:
    if not low or x <= -low[0]:
        heapq.heappush(low, -x)
    else:
        heapq.heappush(high, x)
    if len(low) > len(high) + 1:
        heapq.heappush(high, -heapq.heappop(low))
    elif len(high) > len(low):
        heapq.heappush(low, -heapq.heappop(high))
    out.append(-low[0])
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))
